utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called to order. Good afternoon to everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-14-A, the Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now call for the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, good afternoon, Your Honour. It's Norman Farrell. Ms. Sonja Boelaert-Suominen, Ms. Nicola Bonfield, and Ms. Lourdes Galicia for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that there is a phone link for counsel for the accused. Is that correct? May I have the appearance?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. This is Russell Hayman, appearing by phone from Los Angeles, California. I am here with my colleague Andrew Paley and Anto Nobilo is also appearing from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Now, may I ask Mr. Blaskic if he understands the proceedings, if the translation is correct? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm able to follow these proceedings, and I understand the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaskic. Now, this Status Conference was scheduled for the 22nd of January, 2003, but there were delays due to the appellant's ill health. May I ask whether these health problems have been overcome now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Mr. Hayman. I will ask General Blaskic to address you directly, but first if I could say a few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: First, on behalf of General Blaskic, we would like to thank the Court for its assistance in moving this hearing date because of the appellant's condition. Also, we're pleased to inform the Court that the appellant's condition has improved. It is not normal. He has not returned to a normal state of health, but his health does appear to be improving and it is no longer critical. With that, I would invite him to speak directly to the Court concerning his condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Mr. Blaskic, do you have anything to add to what counsel has just said? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I should like to thank you for your understanding and the understanding of the personnel at the Detention Unit and the medical staff as regards my treatment. However, I must say that I'm not healthy, perfectly healthy yet, but my condition has certainly improved, and it's better than it used to be. I hope that within a month, and following the advice of the doctors and their forecast, I would be fully able to participate in the proceedings and engaged in all other activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Blaskic. I take it that you can follow today the Status Conference without problems. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I can. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaskic. Now, the Status Conference has as its purpose, first, to allow the appellant to express concerns relating to his detention conditions. Are there any further problems besides your health, Mr. Blaskic, that you would like to raise, or that counsel for Mr. Blaskic would like to raise in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Mr. Hayman. We have no concerns regarding the appellant's conditions, but I would also invite him to speak to the Court in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Mr. Blaskic, do you have anything to add? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, except to express my gratitude for the attitude of all of the personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaskic. Let's now then come to the status of this case. I would like to recall first that in October, on the 18th of October exactly, the Prosecution indicated that the review and subsequent disclosure of relevant material would take approximately three and a half months, which has now elapsed. So may I ask if this review and disclosure has been achieved, finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes. The review is -- will be finished as of the end of this week, I anticipate. There were 25 documents that were sent out yesterday. I'm not sure whether the Defence have received them yet. The remaining documents will be reviewed by the end of the week and will either be sent out on Friday or the beginning of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Well, so I get it that this disclosure will be finished very soon, and I don't know whether the -- I ask Mr. Hayman now if the accused has received all the documents and if the review of these documents by the appellant has taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Mr. Hayman. We have not received the 25 documents that Mr. Farrell references having been sent out yesterday from the Prosecutor's offices. I think we will await those documents and review them expeditiously as soon as we receive them, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Well, I would recommend at this stage that the review be done as quickly as possible in order to speed up the consideration of the case now. I hope this could be done very, very shortly. Indeed, I had no other question to raise except that we are expecting the response of the appellant on the Prosecution's rebuttal evidence by next Monday, 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, and it shall be filed on the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Well, then, as soon as this will be done, the Chamber will consider the rebuttal evidence and, if necessary, further submissions that will be made on the basis of disclosed documents, but with the view of taking a final decision on how to proceed in this case. It is the intent of the Appeals Chamber to proceed as speedily as possible on these matters. Are there any other questions that the parties would like to raise? The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the appellant, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Well, that being the situation, this Status Conference may be adjourned, stands adjourned.
